questions.stem: A report must answer questions as fast as possible, and the business is content with figures that are refreshed once each night. Which storage mode fits best?
options: Dual
Import
DirectQuery
A live connection to the source system
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Choose a storage mode

questions.stem: A Product dimension is used both by an imported summary table and by a very large DirectQuery detail table. Which storage mode should the dimension use?
options: DirectQuery
Direct Lake
Dual
Import
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Choose a storage mode

questions.stem: What makes Direct Lake different from both Import and DirectQuery when reading a Delta table in a lakehouse?
options: It translates every DAX query into T-SQL and sends it to the SQL analytics endpoint
It keeps a compressed copy of the data exactly as Import does, but refreshes it more often
It requires the tables to be converted from Delta into a proprietary format first
It loads the Delta files straight into memory without keeping a separate copy and without translating DAX into SQL
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Choose a storage mode

questions.stem: You are asked to describe the shape of a star schema to a colleague who has only ever seen flat spreadsheets. What is the arrangement?
options: One central fact table of measurable events, surrounded by dimension tables that describe them
One table per report page, each holding everything that page needs
A chain of tables where each one relates only to the next
Several fact tables joined directly to each other
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a semantic model

questions.stem: A model contains Product related to Subcategory, which is in turn related to Category. What does star schema guidance recommend doing with those three tables?
options: Relate Category directly to the fact table as well
Turn Subcategory into a second fact table
Leave them as they are, because more tables always mean better compression
Flatten them into a single Product dimension carrying subcategory and category as columns
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a semantic model

questions.stem: A sales fact has both an order date and a ship date, and both need to be sliced by the same date dimension. What is the standard way to model that?
options: Remove the date dimension and use the raw date columns on the fact
Keep one active relationship and activate the other inside a measure with USERELATIONSHIP
Set the second relationship to filter in both directions
Make both relationships active at the same time
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a semantic model

questions.stem: Each customer can hold several accounts and each account can be held by several customers. What do you add to the model to relate them?
options: A bridge table with one row per customer and account pair
A calculated column on each table holding the other table's key
A direct relationship between the two tables filtering both ways
A second copy of the customer table
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement relationships, such as bridge tables and many-to-many relationships

questions.stem: A colleague has set every relationship in the model to filter in both directions because it made one visual work. Why is that a bad default?
options: It converts the model to DirectQuery automatically
It can create ambiguous filter paths and slow queries down
It removes the ability to write measures
It prevents the model from ever being refreshed
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement relationships, such as bridge tables and many-to-many relationships

questions.stem: Two tables already have one active relationship, and you create a second one between the same pair. What does the model do with it?
options: It replaces the first relationship
It is rejected and cannot be created at all
It is created as inactive, and only a measure that names it can use it
It is created active, and the engine picks whichever suits each query
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement relationships, such as bridge tables and many-to-many relationships

questions.stem: The same subexpression appears three times in one measure. What is the main benefit of assigning it to a DAX variable first?
options: It converts the measure into a calculated column
It is evaluated once and reused, which is both clearer and usually faster
It forces the measure to be recalculated on every visual
It allows the measure to ignore all filters
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Write calculations that use DAX variables and functions, such as iterators, table filtering, windowing, and information functions

questions.stem: Revenue must be calculated by multiplying quantity by unit price on each individual sales row and then totalling the result. Which kind of DAX function does that?
options: A filter modifier such as REMOVEFILTERS
An information function such as ISBLANK
An iterator such as SUMX, which evaluates an expression row by row
A simple aggregation such as SUM over a single column
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Write calculations that use DAX variables and functions, such as iterators, table filtering, windowing, and information functions

questions.stem: A measure needs the value from the previous row in whatever order the visual is currently sorted by. Which family of DAX functions is designed for that?
options: Window functions such as OFFSET, which navigate relative to the current row of a result
Filter modifiers, which change which rows are visible
Time intelligence functions, which are the only way to look backwards
Information functions, which report on the current filter context
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Write calculations that use DAX variables and functions, such as iterators, table filtering, windowing, and information functions

questions.stem: Forty measures each need year to date, prior year and year over year variants, and nobody wants to write a hundred and twenty measures. What solves this?
options: A calculation group holding one calculation item per variant
A field parameter listing the forty measures
Forty more measures, generated with a script
A dynamic format string on each measure
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement calculation groups, dynamic format strings, and field parameters

questions.stem: One measure must display as currency when the user selects an amount and as a percentage when they select a ratio. What makes a single measure do that?
options: A dynamic format string, which is a DAX expression returning the format
A calculated column holding the formatted text
Two measures and a bookmark for each state
A conditional formatting rule on the visual
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement calculation groups, dynamic format strings, and field parameters

questions.stem: Users want to choose from a slicer whether a chart is broken down by product, region or channel, without you building three charts. What provides that?
options: A field parameter, which exposes a chosen set of fields as a slicer
Row-level security roles for each breakdown
A calculation group with one item per breakdown
A bookmark for each breakdown, wired to buttons
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement calculation groups, dynamic format strings, and field parameters

questions.stem: What does turning on the large semantic model storage format actually change about a model?
options: It moves the model out of memory and onto disk permanently
It lets the model grow beyond the default size limit, up to the limit of the capacity
It compresses the data more aggressively so the model becomes smaller
It converts every table in the model to DirectQuery
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify use cases for and configure large semantic model storage format

questions.stem: Which of these is a genuine reason to put a semantic model into the large storage format?
options: The model is expected to exceed the default size limit as history accumulates
The source system is slow to query during refresh
The report pages take too long to render
The model needs row-level security
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify use cases for and configure large semantic model storage format

questions.stem: A colleague plans to enable large semantic model storage format on every model in the tenant on the grounds that bigger is safer. What is the honest counterargument?
options: It disables incremental refresh on every model it is applied to
It requires every report to be rebuilt against the model
It permanently prevents those models from being deleted
It is a size setting with no query benefit, so applying it everywhere adds capacity pressure for nothing
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify use cases for and configure large semantic model storage format

questions.stem: What makes a semantic model a composite model rather than an ordinary one?
options: It has been deployed through more than one workspace
It contains more than one fact table
It combines tables in more than one storage mode, or from more than one source
It uses calculation groups as well as measures
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Design and build composite models

questions.stem: You want to extend the certified enterprise sales model with a small budget table of your own, without copying the enterprise model or asking its owners to change it. What do you build, and what do you need?
options: A copy of the enterprise model, which requires Write permission on it
A composite model on top of the enterprise model, which requires Build permission on it
A DirectQuery connection to the enterprise model's underlying warehouse instead
A dataflow that reloads the enterprise model's tables into your workspace
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Design and build composite models

questions.stem: A composite model holds a huge DirectQuery fact table and a small imported table of the same figures summarised by month. How do you make queries use the small one whenever they can?
options: Configure the imported table as a user-defined aggregation over the detail table
Hide the DirectQuery table so users cannot pick it
Set the imported table to dual storage mode
Add a bidirectional relationship between the two tables
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Design and build composite models
